I've (elsewhere) written about this diminishing return effect on LLM utility in relation to increasing expertise.
The question: what's the net positive gain of turning people who know nothing in a given field into sub-novices, while weighing actual experts down with work slop and marginal returns?
And I wonder what the true cost is of arming so many novices with that level of dangerous knowledge. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ![](https://news.ycombinator.com/s.gif) | | [champagnepapi](https://news.ycombinator.com/user?id=champagnepapi) [37 days ago](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49238642) | [root](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49235490) | [parent](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49237593) | [prev](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49238009) | [next](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49235874)[–]
I think the true cost will be some catastrophic failures.
Just hoping folks don’t get hurt due to people not understanding what they’re doing with these things but believing they’re competent. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ![](https://news.ycombinator.com/s.gif) | | [SwtCyber](https://news.ycombinator.com/user?id=SwtCyber) [37 days ago](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49239421) | [parent](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49235490) | [prev](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49237747) | [next](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49238018)[–]

Maybe consider using something else like Brilliant.org if you want to learn a topic, yanno, so you don’t propagate whatever hallucination from ChatGPT to your kids. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ![](https://news.ycombinator.com/s.gif) | | [SwtCyber](https://news.ycombinator.com/user?id=SwtCyber) [37 days ago](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49239407) | [root](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49239268) | [parent](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49239391) | [prev](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49239472) | [next](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49239579)[–]
I think the key difference here is that you're using the LLM to create exercises, not to replace the learning material | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ![](https://news.ycombinator.com/s.gif) | | [wxw](https://news.ycombinator.com/user?id=wxw) [37 days ago](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49235260) | [prev](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49239268) | [next](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49238168)[–]

I'm not sure I follow how this is actually guaranteed? The fact-checking process mentioned just seems to involve asking AI to review its own work. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ![](https://news.ycombinator.com/s.gif) | | [daishi55](https://news.ycombinator.com/user?id=daishi55) [36 days ago](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49246031) | [root](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49235260) | [parent](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49237615) | [next](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49239984)[–]
I mean they have been solved practically I think. I use these things all day every day and haven’t seen a hallucination in a long time. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ![](https://news.ycombinator.com/s.gif) | | [tempacct2cmmnt](https://news.ycombinator.com/user?id=tempacct2cmmnt) [37 days ago](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49235761) | [parent](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49235260) | [prev](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49235483) | [next](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49235719)[–]
Agreed. Given how many significant errors LLMs make in my topic of expertise, despite my taking multiple error checking steps, the idea of catching 100% of hallucinations because you told the LLM to check itself is hilarious. It’s just a wild lack of insight: “I’m using the LLM to teach me something I don’t know about, I definitely have the knowledge base to spot any errors that might remain!” | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ![](https://news.ycombinator.com/s.gif) | | [jack_pp](https://news.ycombinator.com/user?id=jack_pp) [37 days ago](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49243255) | [root](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49235174) | [parent](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49240628) | [next](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49237992)[–]
idk if it's really worsening, someone who has the same issue can apply the patch. I understand why they rejected it but also I'm not willing to learn everything that DS4 did there since I don't plan on working on ffmpeg filters and the knowledge is pretty much useless to me outside this patch. Too much time commitment for.. fixing a filter no one really cared about for 11 years.
But you can see how the parent's comment doesn't really hold, I was able to achieve this while not knowing anything other than what I need fixed and making the LLM test itself towards that goal. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ![](https://news.ycombinator.com/s.gif) | | [ethin](https://news.ycombinator.com/user?id=ethin) [37 days ago](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49236818) | [parent](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49236553) | [next](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49236706)[–]
This is (exactly) why I very strongly tell people not to teach themselves with an LLM. Particularly from the ground up. If you do not understand the domain, you cannot learn from the model because you won't know what questions to ask and it certainly isn't going to answer all of them for you. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ![](https://news.ycombinator.com/s.gif) | | [IshKebab](https://news.ycombinator.com/user?id=IshKebab) [37 days ago](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234885) | [prev](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49236553) | [next](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49234901)[–]
> What you get is a beautiful animation that is 100% accurate and free of hallucinations.
How do you know if you're learning this for the first time? Very risky to learn from LLMs. I've done it, but you have to keep your wits about you. Lots of "oh of course you're right - what I just told you was completely wrong". | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ![](https://news.ycombinator.com/s.gif) | | [dbreunig](https://news.ycombinator.com/user?id=dbreunig) [37 days ago](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49238067) | [prev](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49234901) | [next](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49235521)[–]
> What you get is a beautiful animation that is 100% accurate and free of hallucinations
How does he know? | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ![](https://news.ycombinator.com/s.gif) | | [killingtime74](https://news.ycombinator.com/user?id=killingtime74) [37 days ago](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49238495) | [parent](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49238481) | [next](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49236535)[–]
It's not close to zero. [[https://artificialanalysis.ai/?omniscience=omniscience-hallu](https://artificialanalysis.ai/?omniscience=omniscience-hallu)...](https://artificialanalysis.ai/?omniscience=omniscience-hallucination-rate).
Hallucinations bring to question what you think you've learned. That's going to cost long-term if you labor under mis-apprehensions until you maybe figure out you learned something wrong. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ![](https://news.ycombinator.com/s.gif) | | [zapataband1](https://news.ycombinator.com/user?id=zapataband1) [37 days ago](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49235636) | [prev](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49242409) | [next](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49238462)[–]
"What you get is a beautiful animation that is 100% accurate and free of hallucinations."
Do you know it is free of hallucinations because you crossed checked it with the source material or because you told the LLM "don't hallucinate" | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ![](https://news.ycombinator.com/s.gif) | | [afro88](https://news.ycombinator.com/user?id=afro88) [37 days ago](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49236953) | [prev](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49239083) | [next](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49247876)[–]
I'm all for this and I'm keen to try it. I certainly don't want to take away from sharing another neat use case for learning.
But
> What you get is a beautiful animation that is 100% accurate and free of hallucinations
100% free of hallucinations when you're not an expert that can check it is impossible. LLM hallucinations are an unsolved problem. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ![](https://news.ycombinator.com/s.gif) | | [SwtCyber](https://news.ycombinator.com/user?id=SwtCyber) [37 days ago](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49239380) | [prev](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49239424) | [next](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49234675#49235227)[–]
